Job Category All Clear Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Singapore Health Services Pte Ltd Director (Operations & Admin), Regional Health System Operations Job Category: Administration Posting Date: 21 Sept 2026 The SingHealth Regional Health System (RHS) drives SingHealth's efforts in developing and strengthening partnerships across care providers in the eastern region — both private and public — and across care settings including tertiary, primary and community care. As the central funding conduit for all SingHealth Care Integration and Healthier SG initiatives, RHS provides overarching strategic direction to its programmes, supports service development, and monitors and evaluates key population health initiatives. As Director, you will support the Chief Operating Officer of RHS Operations and clinical site leads, working alongside the SingHealth Office of Regional Health (SORH) to implement population health initiatives, guide mid and long-term strategic planning, and put in place the policy, planning and governance framework to support a future-ready health system through an integrated Community of Care (COC) ecosystem. What You Will Do: You will oversee and coordinate the SingHealth Healthier SG team's service delivery and resource deployment within the COC, while reviewing all services operating under the COC and providing advice and governance on operational issues. In the area of operations and strategic planning, you will work with relevant internal and external stakeholders to formulate, implement and review strategies to deliver value-based care to the population in the eastern region. You will drive and coordinate policies that facilitate population enrolment, and engage process owners and business units to establish business insights that support value-based care and capitation pilot initiatives through data analytics. For the implementation of Next Generation Primary Care, you will engage regional General Practitioners (GPs) and Primary Care Networks (PCNs) to adopt care protocols, programmes, IT systems, and care support and financing arrangements. You will plan and facilitate the regional resident enrolment and service journey, and implement integrated community care teams comprising primary care providers, community nurses, care coordinators and community partners to support residents in adhering to treatment and sustaining behavioural changes that improve their health outcomes. On corporate oversight and governance, you will act as the primary liaison for RHS matters between sites and the RHS group with the Ministry of Health (MOH) and Agency for Integrated Care (AIC), put in place a planning and governance framework to enable monitoring and accountability of key stakeholders, and establish a Risk Management framework to govern the programmes. In the area of performance monitoring and programme evaluation, you will work closely with SingHealth RHS stakeholders to develop key performance indicators, review the progress and effectiveness of RHS initiatives, and recommend improvement plans. Together with Strategic Finance, you will evaluate the cost-effectiveness of right-siting efforts and drive the implementation of the national population health strategy in the capitation funding model to support whole-population enrolment within the eastern region. You will also provide leadership in data analytics to identify needs and areas for improvement. As a partner engagement leader, you will build strong partnerships with internal and external stakeholders to improve health across all age groups, work with sites and institutions to establish system enablers aligned to the cluster's population health strategy, and cultivate strong partnerships with community partners and agencies including MOH, AIC and social and community organisations to drive programmes that promote healthy lifestyle choices. You will also contribute to manpower development by working with the Group Director to develop training programmes that build a core team of staff well versed in population health, and grow a credible pool of staff with competencies and subject matter expertise in this domain. You'll own the frameworks, systems, and relationships that keep NHG aligned with MOH regulations, statutory requirements, and internal policies across the cluster. You'll provide meaningful assurance to senior leadership and Board committees, and play a decisive role in identifying and mitigating compliance risks before they become problems. You'll work across institutions to make sure participation is broad, timely, and meaningful. Turn Data into Insight You'll go beyond reporting numbers — your trend analyses will surface patterns, flag emerging risks, and inform smarter decisions at the leadership level. Institution All Job Function All Job ID All Employment Type All Clear Search Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Create Alert × Select how often (in days) to receive an alert: Apply now » Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource, NUHS@Home Job ID: 10537 Job Function: Administration Institution: National University Health System Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource, NUHS@Home About NUHS@Home NUHS@Home is the National University Health System’s Virtual Campus, a premise-neutral care environment that brings healthcare services beyond the four walls of the hospital and into homes, clinics, community settings, and digital spaces. It serves as the organising platform for multiple virtual and distributed care models, enabling patients to access the right care, at the right time, in the right place. Since its inception in 2020, NUHS@Home has rapidly grown into a critical pillar of NUHS’ vision for healthcare that is integrated, agile, and closer to the patient. More than a single service, it represents a new architecture for care delivery – one where geography no longer dictates access, and recovery happens where patients feel safest, supported, and most at home. The Role We are seeking an experienced, strategic and forward-thinking Senior Manager / Assistant Director, Human Resource . Reporting to the Head of Human Resource, you will serve as a trusted HR leader and strategic business partner to the NUHS@Home leadership team and key stakeholders. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys driving people strategies that support workforce transformation, talent development, employee engagement and organisational growth, while leading the HR team and providing tactical advice and practical solutions across the employee lifecycle. As a key member of the NUHS@Home leadership team, you will play an important role in shaping the people agenda and enabling the continued growth and evolution of the NUHS@Home care delivery model. You will also contribute to leadership continuity for the HR function by supporting the Head of Human Resource on designated matters and strengthening succession coverage within the HR team. What you will own Strategic HR Business Partnering Build strong, trusted relationships with business leaders and stakeholders, providing strategic advice and practical HR solutions that support organisational priorities and business outcomes. Advise leaders on the interpretation and application of HR policies and procedures, employment legislation, performance management, manpower planning, resourcing, rewards and other people-related matters. Partner with Talent Acquisition to develop and implement targeted recruitment strategies aligned with NUHS@Home manpower plans, workforce requirements and growth priorities, including the review and approval of compensation recommendations. Lead the annual manpower planning and budgeting exercise, ensuring alignment with organisational priorities, workforce requirements and financial objectives. Support organisational transformation, change management and workforce redesign initiatives to enable the growth and evolution of NUHS@Home’s care delivery model. Analyse workforce trends, employee engagement data, attrition metrics and other manpower indicators to generate insights and recommendations for organisational and workforce planning, and the effective management of organisational risks. Oversee employee lifecycle matters through the HR team, including employee enquiries, employment changes, transfers, appointments and exit processes, in accordance with HR policies and procedures. People Leadership and Development Lead, manage and develop the HR team to ensure the effective, professional and timely delivery of HR plans, programmes, processes and services. Provide direction, coaching and support to build HR capability, strengthen service delivery and promote a high-performing team culture. Foster close collaboration with relevant Group HR Centres of Excellence to deliver integrated and value-adding people solutions. Employee Engagement, Talent and Workforce Development Drive employee engagement initiatives that strengthen workplace culture, employee experience, productivity and retention. Work with leaders to identify organisational capability gaps and support organisation design, workforce planning, capability-building and talent pipeline initiatives. Promote a culture of continuous learning, collaboration, accountability and service excellence. Governance, Policy and Stakeholder Collaboration Collaborate with NUHS Group HR Centres of Excellence and relevant stakeholders to implement HR projects, programmes and initiatives. Work with the Centres of Excellence to review and enhance HR policies, guidelines and processes to ensure their relevance to NUHS@Home and compliance with applicable regulatory requirements. Contribute to NUHS, Ministry of Manpower (MOM), Ministry of Health (MOH), MOH Holdings (MOHH), NUHS@Home and Human Resource projects, events, governance initiatives, policy reviews and committees, as assigned or appointed. Who You Are This role is suited to an experienced HR leader who is able to operate at both strategic and operational levels: shaping the people agenda, advising senior stakeholders, leading a small HR team, and translating organisational priorities into practical workforce and talent solutions. Background A bachelor’s degree in Human Resource Management, Business Management or a related discipline. At least 10 years of relevant HR experience, preferably within the healthcare sector, with a strong track record in HR business partnering, organisational transformation, workforce redesign and people management. Demonstrated ability to influence and partner with business leaders to achieve strategic business and people outcomes. Demonstrated experience leading, coaching and developing HR professionals or business partners. Strong knowledge of HR practices, including employee relations, performance management, manpower planning, talent management, resourcing and rewards. Proven leadership and collaboration skills, with the ability to develop team members, build effective partnerships across functions and work independently with a high degree of initiative. Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills, with the ability to translate workforce data and insights into actionable recommendations. Proficient in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel and PowerPoint, with experience in workforce analytics, manpower reporting, budgeting and presentation development. Experience in healthcare operations, change management or organisational capability-building would be an advantage. What we offer An opportunity to help shape NUHS’ healthcare workforce of the future and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore. Meaningful ownership and decision-making responsibility in a high-growth healthcare transformation programme. The opportunity to contribute to the development of NUHS@Home and its future leadership capability as the programme scales. Why Join Us NUHS@Home is redefining care delivery by creating Singapore’s virtual campus for comprehensive clinical care through a digital-first approach. You will contribute to workforce transformation and the future of healthcare delivery in Singapore and beyond. As part of the Private Mobility team, you are expected to work together with other government agencies to: • Develop and review private mobility strategies and policies, such as on the Certificate of Entitlement; • Develop measures to contribute to the transport sector’s move towards sustainability, including measures to scale up electric vehicle adoption; • Study trends that may impact the future of transport and develop proposals to enable Singapore to stay ahead of these trends; and • Engage international and local thought leaders from both the private and public sectors, as well as help spur industry development efforts. Candidates should possess strong critical thinking skills, intellectual curiosity, excellent writing, verbal communication, and interpersonal skills. Candidates should be able to work independently, and be confident in analysing qualitative and quantitative information.

This is a purposeful role that offers opportunities to co-create and co-deliver solutions that better support migrant workers (MWs) and migrant domestic workers (MDWs). We are looking for a dynamic and experienced leader to join the team as Senior Assistant Director. The successful candidate will lead Engagement and Partnerships work within CEPD, overseeing strategies, programmes and stakeholder relationships that strengthen the ecosystem of support for MWs and MDWs. As team lead for Engagement and Partnerships, you will develop strategies to engage and collaborate with key stakeholders, including community partners, employers, schools, government agencies and foreign embassies. You will also work closely with MOM departments and external agencies to develop programmes, secure resourcing, and oversee implementation. The role also involves leading a multi-functional team responsible for co-creating and co-delivering initiatives such as socio-recreational activities, training and employment pathways, well-being assistance, and alternative rest spaces or meaningful off-day programmes for MDWs. You will help deepen existing partnerships, onboard new partners, and foster co-ownership of solutions that are grounded in the lived experiences of migrants.
